newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Coca-Cola to invest $60 mln in Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola to invest $60 mln in Zimbabwe.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co will invest $60 million in Zimbabwe over the next four years with the aim of doubling its business in the southern African country, the soft drinks company announced on Wednesday.

Company president Douglas Ivestor said, "We're committed to helping drive long-term economic growth in Zimbabwe. The market conditions we see now position Zimbabwe as the next centre of growth for our busineses on the African continent."
Ivestor met Zimbabwe president Robert Mugabe at the president's residence on Tuesday morning to brief him on the U.S. company's investment plan.

"Our meeting with the President went very well. We're delighted to be doing business in Zimbabwe and delighted to announce the expansion of our business here. He (Mugabe) seemed very pleased," Ivestor told reporters.

The news follows Monday's announcement by Coca-Cola of plans to invest more than one billion rand ($220 million) in South Africa. The company said with further spending in other African countries it planned total investments of $500 million for sub-Saharan Africa.
"We're very positive on Africa as a whole," Ivestor said.
Through its new investment in Zimbabwe, Coca-Cola plans to expand operations and increase capacity at Zimbabwe's five Coca-Cola bottling plants.

"It will purchase new production lines, packaging, cold drink equipment and other sales equipment to satisfy a growing consumer thirst for Coca-Cola products across the nation," Coca-Cola said in a statement.

Coca-Cola was first established in Zimbabwe in 1948. In 1996 total sales of the company's softdrinks climbed 10 percent from the previous year, to more than 30 million cases or a market share of 85 percent.
Ivestor said the investment programme would also benefit some 17,000 retailers, kiosk operators and trolley vendors.
"(We are investing in) things that empower people that want to go into business," Ivestor said.
Coca-Cola currently employs more than 2,300 people in Zimbabwe. The company said that for every job it provided about five additional jobs were created in the local economy.
Zimbabwe, with a population of 11.5 million, is the fourth largest sub-Saharan market for Coca-Cola.
The company plans investment of $30 million for Tanzania, $30 million for Uganda, $10 million for Ethiopia and investments in Mozambique and Kenya.
